objectives.description: Locate ordinary pain or injury with bounded anatomy labels.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions1.1 body and13.2/13.3 B1 versus B2; A1/A2 earlier comparison
objectives.rationale: Bounded pain/impact locations enumerate the six inherited neck/shoulder/chest/knee/heart/blood B1 hypotheses and add joint, skin, bone/muscle and common-organ contrasts needed by the selected account. Prior A1/A2 body locations remain prerequisites; no exhaustive anatomy or diagnostic competence is implied.

objectives.description: Describe the bodily action immediately before or after an ordinary accident.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions1.3 bodily actions and13.2 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Fall, stumble/slip, physical contact, release/hold, jump, movement, breathing/crying/kissing and selected posture changes have explicit meanings. Standing/seated and routine walking/sitting are inherited. F general actions and literal versus musical/digital polysemy are resolved as proposals, not automatically merged.

objectives.description: Describe a person's visible change or resemblance neutrally.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions1.2/13.7 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Resemblance, gaze, outward appearance, posture, tactile skin and weight-change descriptions complement earlier hair/build descriptors. Changes are self-described or plainly observable without medical judgement; body weight never determines value or health advice.

objectives.description: Describe ordinary life transitions and personal development.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions1.4 life cycle and3.1.6 age B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Personal history covers birth/lifetime/death, childhood/newborn references and optional neutral pregnancy/childbirth/menstruation and sexual-health labels. Earlier birth/growth/death verbs remain prerequisites. Detailed reproduction, treatment and exhaustive life-stage taxonomy are not required for the selected ordinary account.

objectives.description: Update or describe personal identity without forcing disclosure.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions3.1–3.3 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Earlier name/address/nationality/document fields are prerequisites, with residence change reused. Selected diary/photo collection and optional identity/orientation/gender labels support personal descriptions without required disclosure or an exhaustive identity taxonomy. T/W own document processes.

objectives.description: Describe household relationships and changes in family life.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions4.1/3.1.8 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Cohabitation, familiar in-laws, adoption, couple status changes, dating/breakup and anniversaries/congratulations are explicitly selected. Earlier close relatives/marital-state/gift/celebration and getting-along meanings remain required; no relationship form is assumed superior or legally equivalent.

objectives.description: Explain interpersonal disagreement and restoration of a relationship.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions4.2/4.4 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Disagreement, misunderstanding, trust, apology, forgiveness, reconciliation, responsibility, commitment and support provide the selected breakdown/repair account. Restoring a relationship, agreeing on a proposition and solving a problem remain different. No instruction to tolerate harm or forgive is given.

objectives.description: Describe causes and consequences of ordinary feelings.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions2.1–2.3 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: The selected ordinary reaction set links blocked expectations, worry, gladness/sadness, relief, disappointment, embarrassment/pride, fright/pressure/motivation and emotional hurt with causes and consequences. Earlier emotion states/transitions are inherited. Derived nouns and metaphorical pain uses have unresolved granularity rather than automatic new counts.

objectives.description: Describe noticing, recalling and interpreting an ordinary personal experience.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions2.4 and8 general notions7; B1/B2 comparison
objectives.rationale: Lived-event experience is explicitly different from baseline practical knowledge. Noticing, realization, memory, adaptation and inattention support personal narration; exact five planned experience senses and high-risk temporal/result baselines are individually reconciled. General F temporal/cause/stance systems are prerequisites.

objectives.description: Describe interpersonal conduct, values and habits with ordinary precision.

Earlier P personality/value adjectives and A2 S respect are reused; clinical personality analysis and exhaustive trait taxonomies are outside this scenario.

objectives.description: Describe an ordinary accident and identify the resulting injury.
frameworkSections: 9 specific notions13.2 B1 versus B2
objectives.rationale: Finite ordinary accident contrasts enumerate fall/slip/stumble, impact, cut/burn/open injury/bruise/fracture/sprain and visible bleeding/swelling consequences. All are descriptive or already reported labels. Body-middle constructions versus general physical break remain unresolved; no diagnosis, triage threshold or treatment procedure.

A2 curar/cuidar/mejorar/empeorar retain their meanings; reflexivity does not automatically create a B1 word.
